Plot a Fitted qtlAim Object

Source: R/plot.qtlAim.R
plot.qtlAim.Rd

Produces one of six diagnostic or results plots for a qtlAim object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'qtlAim'
plot(
  x,
  genObj,
  type = c("outlier", "blups", "chr", "effects", "contrast", "heatmap"),
  data = NULL,
  iter = NULL,
  chr = NULL,
  chr.lines = FALSE,
  sig.col = "firebrick",
  pt.col = NULL,
  pt.cex = 0.6,
  cap = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A qtlAim object.

genObj

The "wgCross" object passed to qtlAim, produced by primeCross.

type

Character string selecting the plot type:

"outlier" (default)

Line plot of genome-wide interval/marker outlier statistics \(\tilde{q}_i^2/\tilde{v}_i\), one facet per iteration. Detected QTL are annotated.

"blups"

Line plot of genome-wide scaled BLUPs \(\tilde{q}_i / \sqrt{|\tilde{v}_i|}\), one facet per iteration.

"chr"

Chromosome-level aggregated outlier statistics as a bar chart (only when qtlAim was run with selection = "chromosome").

"effects"

Lollipop plot of estimated additive effect sizes for each detected QTL, with \(\pm\) 1 SE error bars, percentage of phenotypic variance explained annotated on each head, and allele direction (A / B; or 0/1/2 for GWAS panels) colour-coded.

"contrast"

Allele contrast plot: for each detected QTL one facet shows the distribution of total line genetic values (additive genomic BLUP + residual genetic BLUP + QTL fixed contributions) split by allele class. Requires data (the phenotypic data frame used in the analysis). Biparental populations use A / AB / B classes; GWAS panels use 0 / 1 / 2 dosage classes.

"heatmap"

Genome x iteration heatmap: tile fill encodes the outlier statistic \(\tilde{q}_i^2/\tilde{v}_i\) at every interval/marker position across all forward-selection iterations. Positions excluded by the exclusion window are shown in grey. Detected QTL are marked with a filled diamond at the (position, iteration) cell where they were selected. Iteration 1 is at the top. Useful for seeing where genome-wide signal builds, dissipates, or shifts as each QTL is absorbed into the model.

data

Data frame. The phenotypic data used in the analysis (the <response>.data object created by qtlAim / gwasAim in the calling environment). Required only when type = "contrast".

iter

Integer vector of iterations to display. Default is all stored iterations. Not used for "effects" or "contrast".

chr

Optional character vector of chromosome names to display. Not used for "effects" or "contrast".

chr.lines

Logical. If TRUE, vertical lines are drawn at chromosome boundaries ("outlier" and "blups" only). Default FALSE.

sig.col

Colour used to highlight and label the selected QTL in each iteration facet ("outlier" / "blups" / "chr" types). Default "firebrick".

pt.col

Character vector of length equal to the number of displayed chromosomes, or length 2 for alternating colours. Colours the line/rug traces by chromosome. Default uses hcl.colors.

pt.cex

Numeric line/point width. Default 0.6.

cap

Numeric scalar. Upper limit for the colour scale in type = "heatmap". Outlier statistics above this value are clamped to cap and rendered in the maximum colour, stretching the gradient across the lower range where most signal variation occurs. Default NULL (no capping; full data range used). Not used for other plot types.

...

Additional optional arguments for specific plot types.

ncol

Integer. Number of facet columns for type = "contrast". Default 1L (vertical stack).

qtl

Integer vector. Index (genome order) of QTL to show in type = "contrast". Default NULL (all QTL).

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

qtlAim, summary.qtlAim, aimTrace, linkMap.qtlAim

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot(qtl.fit, genObj = genoRxK)
plot(qtl.fit, genObj = genoRxK, type = "effects")
plot(qtl.fit, genObj = genoRxK, type = "heatmap")
plot(qtl.fit, genObj = genoRxK, type = "contrast", data = yld.data)
} # }
